title: Decidability and completeness of concurrent Kleene algebra with parallel iteration
formal: Settle both parts of the source question for the full concurrent Kleene-algebra signature, including unbounded finite parallel iteration. For finite expressions \(e,f\), write \(e\preceq f\) when \(\downarrow\llbracket e\rrbracket\subseteq\downarrow\llbracket f\rrbracket\), using the pomset refinement semantics below. (1) Is there a total computable procedure deciding \(e\preceq f\) on every pair of such expressions? (2) Are the stated Kleene-algebra axioms for both products, together with weak interchange, complete for this semantics: \[\forall e,f,\quad e\preceq f\ \Longrightarrow\ \mathsf{CKA}\vdash e+f=f?\] The already settled fragment without parallel iteration is recorded in the context. The two remaining questions are separate: neither an algorithm alone nor an axiomatic completeness theorem alone is a complete answer to this paired target.

source_formulation.text: For expressions with sequential and parallel iteration, determine decidability of refinement by inclusion of downward-closed pomset languages and completeness of concurrent Kleene algebra with weak interchange.
source_formulation.caption: Editorial paraphrase of the full-signature questions; settled fragment identified in context

why: The two questions ask whether unrestricted finite spawning of concurrent computations remains algorithmically comparable, and whether every valid refinement can be justified by a fixed algebraic calculus. Parallel iteration crosses the bounded-width boundary where existing decision and completeness results apply. Resolving the full signature would clarify the expressive and proof-theoretic cost of unbounded concurrency.
status_note: The CONCUR 2017 source’s own EXPSPACE theorem and ESOP 2018 completeness theorem settle the signature without parallel star. The full signature’s completeness is explicitly retained in Kappé’s 2020 thesis, p. 132. Bounded later-work checking through 16 September 2026, including CONCUR 2026 Article 42, found no matching full-signature resolution of either target. This source-open assessment is not a proof that no later result exists, and generic continuous-model completeness is not identified with the stated finitary axiomatic completeness.

progress.text: The source cites full bi-Kleene language-equivalence decidability and completeness without the interchange/refinement semantics.
The source proves EXPSPACE-completeness of refinement for expressions without parallel iteration; full series-parallel rational refinement is outside that decision theorem.
The ESOP paper proves completeness for concurrent Kleene algebra with bounded parallelism and explicitly excludes parallel star.
The thesis’s Parallel Star further-work subsection retains full-signature axiomatic completeness as an unresolved extension.
The checked CONCUR paper develops continuous-model semantics and modular tools for specific hypotheses, without a matching resolution of both full-signature targets.

importance.reason: A central boundary for algebraic reasoning about concurrent behavior: both stars and interchange are individually natural, but together exceed the bounded-parallelism results. Retaining both decidability and completeness preserves the source’s distinct computational and proof-theoretic targets.

sentences: Concurrent Kleene algebra describes finite partially ordered executions using choice, sequential and parallel composition, and iteration.
The card asks both whether refinement is decidable and whether its valid inequalities follow from the stated axioms when both sequential and parallel iteration are allowed.
Refinement preserves events and labels while permitting extra ordering, and parallel iteration allows arbitrarily many concurrent copies.
Decision and completeness results for expressions without parallel iteration do not settle the full-signature questions retained here.
A resolution would establish the algorithmic and proof-theoretic limits of algebraic reasoning about unbounded finite concurrency.

definitions:
An input supplies a finite alphabet \(\Sigma\) and two finite syntax trees generated by \[e ::= 0\mid1\mid a\ (a\in\Sigma)\mid e+e\mid e\cdot e\mid e\parallel e\mid e^*\mid e^\dagger.\] The alphabet and syntax trees have explicit finite encodings, with labels represented by binary indices; no succinctly shared circuits, numerical iteration counts or bound on nesting is imposed. A pomset is a finite partially ordered set of events labelled in \(\Sigma\), considered up to label-preserving order isomorphism. The empty pomset interprets \(1\), the singleton labelled \(a\) interprets \(a\), and \(0\) denotes the empty language. A sequential product \(P\cdot Q\) uses disjoint copies and places every event of \(P\) before every event of \(Q\); a parallel product \(P\parallel Q\) uses disjoint copies with no additional cross-order. Lift products to sets by taking every pair, and interpret \(+\) as union. The language of \(e^*\) is the union of all finite sequential products of members of \(\llbracket e\rrbracket\); \(e^\dagger\) is the analogous union of finite parallel products. Both include the empty product. These are finite executions of unbounded size, not infinite executions. A pomset \(P\) refines \(Q\), written \(P\sqsubseteq Q\), if there is a bijection from the events of \(Q\) to those of \(P\) preserving labels and every order comparison in \(Q\); \(P\) may add further comparisons. Put \(\downarrow L=\{P:\exists Q\in L,\ P\sqsubseteq Q\}\), ranging over all finite pomsets. Thus \(e\preceq f\) equivalently says every pomset of \(\llbracket e\rrbracket\) refines some pomset of \(\llbracket f\rrbracket\). For example, \(a\cdot b\preceq a\parallel b\).

The proof system \(\mathsf{CKA}\) uses ordinary finite equational reasoning (reflexivity, symmetry, transitivity, substitution and congruence) and the following axiom and inference schemas on arbitrary full-signature terms. Write \(x\le y\) as an abbreviation for \(x+y=y\). Addition is associative, commutative and idempotent, with identity \(0\). For each pair \((\circ,\star)\in\{(\cdot,*),(\parallel,\dagger)\}\), the product is associative, has identity \(1\), has absorbing element \(0\), distributes over addition on both sides, and satisfies \[1+x\circ x^\star=x^\star=1+x^\star\circ x.\] Its induction rules are \[x\circ y\le y\ \Longrightarrow\ x^\star\circ y\le y,\qquad y\circ x\le y\ \Longrightarrow\ y\circ x^\star\le y.\] Parallel product additionally commutes. Finally impose weak interchange \[(x\parallel z)\cdot(y\parallel w)\le(x\cdot y)\parallel(z\cdot w).\] Premises of induction rules must themselves be derived; no extra assumptions about the input letters are available. Soundness holds for the downward-closed pomset semantics. The decision question requires exact deterministic halting answers, with no error allowance, oracle or complexity bound.
answer_criterion: Provide complete Lean-checked resolutions of both parts, with a separate conclusion for each. Decidability requires a total computable classifier for the displayed semantic preorder and a correctness proof; undecidability requires a proof that no such classifier exists. Completeness requires derivability of every valid refinement inequality from exactly the stated finite-proof schemas. Incompleteness requires a valid inequality and a proof of its nonderivability, for example through a fully verified algebraic countermodel to derivability. A proof for terms omitting \(\dagger\), or for plain language equality before refinement closure, is partial. A theorem about validity in all continuous models does not by itself prove completeness of the specified finitary axioms.

context_blocks.text: A pomset records which events must precede which other events. Refinement adds ordering constraints while preserving all events and labels. It can turn parallel behavior into more sequential behavior; it cannot delete an event or arbitrarily rename its action.

The operation \(e^\dagger\) permits any finite number of copies of \(e\) to run in parallel. Even the expression \(a^\dagger\) has executions with arbitrarily many mutually unordered events. Expressions without this operation have a width bound depending on their syntax, even when sequential star permits executions of unbounded length.

The source’s introductory paragraph recalls both the general question and its bounded-width fragment. Its own Theorem 26 then proves that refinement of series-rational expressions, without parallel star, is EXPSPACE-complete. The imported excerpt stopped before that result, so it was misleading to leave the whole historical paragraph marked unreviewed and open.

Laurence and Struth establish completeness and decidability for equality of full bi-Kleene pomset languages, before adding refinement closure. Their bounded-width refinement theorem and the ESOP 2018 result establish completeness in the smaller signature. None of these theorems removes the parallel-iteration qualification in the active question.

The ESOP 2018 paper explicitly omits parallel star. Its conclusion shows why its syntactic closure method cannot simply be reused: refinement closure of a parallel iteration can contain series-parallel pomsets with arbitrarily deep alternation of sequential and parallel composition, beyond any single plain series-parallel rational expression. This obstruction to one method is not a proof of undecidability or incompleteness.

The 2020 thesis retains the parallel-star completeness issue in its further-work section. Its extended correspondence between expressions and pomset automata is a different theorem: representing an expression by an automaton does not automatically decide refinement between the represented languages.

The August 2026 paper gives a broad semantics for continuous algebras with hypotheses and tools for particular axiomatic completeness proofs. It explicitly separates canonical model completeness from completeness of finitary axioms. The checked results do not supply a full parallel-star refinement decider or a proof of completeness of the exact calculus stated here.
